Answer: F
Reason: The sagittal CT images (Figures 1, 2, 5) clearly demonstrate a focal outpouching (pseudoaneurysm) at the aortic isthmus/distal to the left subclavian artery and an intimal flap in the descending thoracic aorta, consistent with traumatic aortic injury. Additionally, Figure 4 shows patchy opacities in the left lung indicative of pulmonary contusion, making Option F the most accurate description of the combined findings.
